clue.text: Almost without section in corset, slow to turn (12, three words)

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the final letter of the word built here is dropped

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for section
lacking means without
stays are an old-fashioned corset stiffened with bones

explanation.surface: A woman too slow to turn round, hampered by a corset with a panel missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without section' is read as 'section-lacking'; 'Almost' trims the last letter of that phrase. Stays are an old boned corset.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack in stays is a sailing term for a vessel that is sluggish in going about, that is, slow to come round onto the other tack.

clue.text: Drill having run for nothing in black stone

indicators.note: one thing for another means the first takes the place of the second

parts.note: to drill pupils is to school them
R is the abbreviation for run
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A drill bores through black stone, one run made for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drill' looks like a boring tool, but it means train; the second O of SCHOOL gives way to R.
explanation.definitionFit: Schorl is black tourmaline, a glossy black mineral.

clue.text: Left gilded, one winning top prize

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
aureate means golden or gilded

explanation.surface: Gilded and left on a pedestal: the fate of a champion who takes the top prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A laureate is someone honoured with an award, such as a Nobel laureate, so a winner of a top prize.

clue.text: Chinese pottery? Depression rises with cheat around

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: to con is to cheat or swindle

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading from bottom to top, so the word is backwards

parts.note: a dale is a valley, a depression in the land

explanation.surface: A depressed dealer in Chinese porcelain is cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is there because celadon is strictly the glaze, not the pottery itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Celadon is a pale grey-green glaze first made in China, and the stoneware decorated with it.

clue.text: Ceremonial gift, trimmed hat accepted in reverse of pompous speech

indicators.note: something accepted in is taken inside, so one piece sits within the other
the reverse of a word is that word read backwards

parts.note: talk in the sense of grand or empty talk, as in big talk

indicators.note: trimming cuts off an edge, here the last letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: At a ceremony, a pompous speaker accepts a gift of a hat that has been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimmed hat lands just after the first letter of the backward speech. Talk as pompous speech is a loose fit, in the sense of big talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A khalat, or khilat, is a robe of honour presented by an Eastern ruler as a mark of favour, a ceremonial gift.

clue.text: I lost in wacky carnival, having to concede award after sea fight (10, two words)

indicators.note: wacky means crazy, so the letters are put in a mad new order
something lost has gone missing, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: the letter to be removed
taken as written
to own up is to concede or admit

explanation.surface: Losing at a crazy carnival, someone has to give up a prize after a mock sea battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concede award' looks like a phrase, but 'concede' gives OWN and 'award' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval crown is a gold crown decorated with ships' prows, given in ancient Rome to the first man to board an enemy ship in a sea battle.

clue.text: Insecticide? Time of death involves millions — and it's all up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the whole thing runs backwards
to involve is to wrap up or include, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: obit is an old word for death or its anniversary
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: An insecticide brings death to millions of bugs, and then it's all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's all up' sounds like 'it's all over', but in a down clue it turns the whole assembly upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbo is a South American climbing plant whose roots yield a poison used to kill insects and stun fish; the question mark marks the plant-for-product stretch.

clue.text: Ecstasy in action unusually felt but not understood

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so these letters are set out in an uncommon order

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
taken as written

explanation.surface: On ecstasy, a clubber feels everything strangely but understands nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ecstasy' is not the feeling but the drug, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Anoetic describes consciousness that is experienced as sensation without being grasped by thought, so felt but not understood.

clue.text: Piglet set free, violent penned

indicators.note: penned means shut in a pen, so this piece goes inside the other
letters set free are released from their order and can move about

parts.note: taken as written
hot as in a hot temper, fierce or violent

explanation.surface: A piglet is let out of its pen, while a violent one stays shut in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set free' looks like the piglet escaping, but 'free' is the signal to rearrange the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shotte is a variant of shote or shott, a young pig recently weaned.

clue.text: Bulbous SA plant: you'll find each in patchy ground

indicators.note: ground here is the past tense of grind, so these letters are crushed and remade

parts.note: the twelve letters used as written

explanation.surface: A gardener explains where a South African bulb grows: dotted around in uneven, patchy soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like soil in the surface, but it is the past tense of grind, and the twelve letters of 'each in patchy' are its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cape hyacinth (Galtonia) is a tall summer-flowering bulb native to South Africa, the Cape being its home region.

clue.text: Remove covering of bottom?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to strip the husk or pod from peas, beans or grain
second meaning: the body or bottom of a ship

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like taking the clothes off someone's backside; the question mark warns that 'bottom' is the nautical one.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to husk or shell; as a noun it is the main body of a ship below the deck, its bottom.

clue.text: No. 5 trapped, one run out in period of play at MCG?

indicators.note: something trapped is caught and held inside, so one piece is shut within the others

parts.note: a means one
R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for run
O is the abbreviation for out on a cricket scorecard
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the number five batsman trapped lbw and another run out during a session at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words are all doing letter duty; the Roman five sits inside A, R and O. MCG is the Melbourne Cricket Ground, pointing to Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Arvo is Australian slang for afternoon, and the afternoon is one of the sessions into which a day's cricket in Melbourne is divided.

clue.text: Tedious US job making one fret and go haywire in time of expansion (10, two words)

parts.note: to fret is to chafe or rub

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a boom is a period of rapid economic growth
to err is to go wrong

explanation.surface: A boring American job, the kind that makes a person fret and go mad, even in boom times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fret' is the verb to chafe, not to worry, and 'making one' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In New York a rubber room was a reassignment centre where suspended teachers sat idle on full pay all day, a tedious posting.

clue.text: Magic mumbo-jumbo emitting same string twice

indicators.note: emitting means sending out, and the same run of letters goes out on both occasions it appears

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A conjuror's patter gives off the same incantation twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated string is UMB, found once in each half of mumbo-jumbo; take it out of both and M-O-J-O is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Mojo is a charm or spell from African-American folk belief, so magical power in general.

clue.text: Ancient herb verse has spoken about

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round the other

parts.note: oral means spoken rather than written
V is the abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: An old poem praising some ancient herb has been recited aloud about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as 'verse has spoken about it': ORAL wraps round V.
explanation.definitionFit: Orval is an obsolete name for clary, a sage grown since antiquity as a medicinal herb.

clue.text: Even though settled having to live in

indicators.note: having one thing in another means the first is held inside the second

parts.note: alit is a past tense of alight, to settle or land
to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: Someone has moved in somewhere, even though they've only just settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled' is the past tense of alight, as a bird settles on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Albeit is a formal conjunction meaning although, introducing a concession.

clue.text: Catching a fish, spun reel — OK for passing the time on holiday?

definitions.text: OK for passing the time on holiday?

indicators.note: catching means taking hold of, so the outer letters close round the next ones
something spun is whirled about, so these letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the dab is a small flatfish

explanation.surface: An angler on holiday spins the reel and lands a fish: pleasant enough for whiling away a few hours.
explanation.walkthrough: The fishing scene hides two signals in 'Catching' and 'spun'; the fish is the small flatfish, not a generic catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A readable book is one good enough to pass the time with, the sort of novel taken on holiday; the question mark admits the example.

clue.text: Jellyfish? Beth's neighbour gets nipped by one

indicators.note: something nipped is pinched between two jaws, so the other piece closes round it

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice
beth is the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet, and aleph is the first, beside it

explanation.surface: A jellyfish story: Beth's neighbour gets stung by one while swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: Beth is not a woman but a Hebrew letter, so her neighbour is ALEPH.
explanation.definitionFit: Acalephe is an old zoological name for a jellyfish or similar stinging sea creature; the question mark marks the dated term.

clue.text: Nodding dogs? They're regularly trodden on

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: toy dogs on the back shelf of a car are pets kept in a car
second meaning: floor coverings walked on every day

explanation.walkthrough: Nodding dogs are toy dogs whose heads bob on a car's rear shelf, a British fad; split the answer as CAR PETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Toy dogs riding in a car are jokingly its pets, while carpets are floor coverings that people constantly walk over.

clue.text: Fruit, funny on end of nose

parts.note: comic means funny

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word nose

explanation.surface: A comedy prop: a fruit stuck comically on the tip of a clown's nose.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: Comice is a variety of dessert pear, sweet and juicy, so a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Masters ensuring a term is varied

indicators.note: varied means changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the seven letters used as written

explanation.surface: School masters make sure each term is different from the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri is the Italian plural of maestro, an eminent musician or master of an art.

clue.text: Attitude showing I'd turned away from opposition?

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the short word is read backwards
taking something away from a word removes those letters from it

parts.note: the contraction written without its apostrophe
distance in the old sense of disagreement or estrangement, as Shakespeare used it

explanation.surface: Someone whose attitude shows they've moved away from the opposition party.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed I'd, DI, is the opening of DISTANCE; strip it off and the answer is left. Distance meaning discord is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a standpoint or position taken on an issue, which is an attitude.

clue.text: Divination classes, including opening of e.g. epic

indicators.note: including means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sorts are kinds or classes

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word epic

explanation.surface: Fortune-telling classes that include opening an epic such as the Aeneid at random.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: the best-known form opened Virgil's epic at random for a prophecy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sortes is divination by chance selection, especially by picking a random passage from a book such as Virgil or the Bible.

clue.text: Saliva limits activity in end of pipe

indicators.note: limits here is a verb, to bound or enclose, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: spit is saliva
go means energy or activity, as in full of go

explanation.surface: A pipe smoker's spit gathers at the mouthpiece and slows everything down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limits' reads as a noun, boundaries, but it is a verb: SPIT holds GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is the plain end of a pipe that fits into the socket of the next one, or a tap at a pipe's end.

clue.text: Name, reverse of rude, for Asiatic trees

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read from end to start

parts.note: sassy means cheeky or impudent

explanation.surface: A botanist offers a name for some Asian trees that is the opposite of rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse of rude' looks like a call for an antonym such as polite, but it means a rude word written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyssa is a genus of trees, the tupelos, with species native to eastern Asia as well as North America.

clue.text: He ruled in Tirana, prince in the end overthrown?

indicators.note: something overthrown is turned upside down, which in a down clue means read backwards
one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a term is an end or limit, as in the term of a lease
P is the abbreviation for prince

explanation.surface: An Albanian ruler, the prince, was finally overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' looks like 'finally', but it places P inside TERM. Tirana is the capital of Albania.
explanation.definitionFit: Mpret, Albanian for king, was the title taken by Prince Wilhelm of Wied, who briefly ruled Albania from Durrës in 1914.

clue.text: One catching horses has to work steadily at corralling in strict fashion

indicators.note: corralling means penning animals in an enclosure, so one piece is shut inside the other

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work steadily at it
a roper is a cowboy who lassoes horses or cattle

explanation.surface: A cowboy rounding up horses must keep working steadily, herding them into the pen by the book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One catching horses' looks like the definition of the whole answer, but it is only the inner piece, penned inside PLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Properly can mean strictly or in the strict sense, as in 'properly speaking'.

clue.text: Great old-fashioned romance, one to raise the spirits?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an archaic word for a whopping lie, romance here being a fanciful untruth
second meaning: a medium who calls up ghosts that answer by knocking

explanation.walkthrough: 'Romance' is not love but a tall story, and 'Great' tells you it is a big one. The spirits raised are ghosts, not moods.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists the word as an old term for a great lie, and a spirit-rapper is a medium who communicates with the dead by knocks.

clue.text: End of the road in song is dyke?

definitions.text: End of the road in song

parts.note: taken as written
les is a slang word for a lesbian, as is dyke

explanation.surface: A question about where the road finishes in some song: is it at a dyke?
explanation.walkthrough: The song is the Scottish 'Road to the Isles', so its road ends at the islands. 'Dyke' looks like a wall or ditch at the road's end, but it is slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The Road to the Isles is a Scottish song about walking to the Hebrides, so the destination where that road finishes is the islands.

clue.text: Row: it goes on when making cookies with mom?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a line or level, as of seats rising one above another

definitions.text: it goes on when making cookies with mom?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an American word for a child's pinafore, put on to keep clothes clean while baking

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cookies' and 'mom' are the American signals: the second meaning is a US word for a child's apron or pinafore.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows placed one above another; in American usage it is also a child's pinafore.

clue.text: What seals give emitting din, a deep sound

indicators.note: emitting means sending out, so the named letters leave the word

parts.note: a seal, whether glue or wax, provides bonding
taken as written, the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: What noise do seals make? They let out a din, a deep honking sound.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures barking seals, but these seals are things that stick; remove the din from the middle of BONDING.
explanation.definitionFit: A bong is the resonant, low note of a large bell or gong.

clue.text: Excellent performance? Reverse of that

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read from its last letter back to its first

parts.note: a spot is a performer's slot or turn in a show

explanation.surface: Was it an excellent performance, or the exact opposite?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excellent performance' wants to be one phrase, but the clue splits after 'Excellent'; the reverse is of the word for the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tops is informal for the very best, as in 'the show was tops'.

clue.text: Hurray! Advertising video returns following record: Seaweeds

parts.note: to enter details is to record them

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so these letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ah is an exclamation of pleasure or delight
a promo is a short promotional video

explanation.surface: Hooray! The advert has come back on after the record finished: something about seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal takes both the exclamation and the advertising video together, and the result follows ENTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteromorpha is a genus of green algae, the gut weeds, so the name covers a group of seaweeds.

clue.text: Sets in order — messiest stay disorganized

indicators.note: disorganized means thrown out of order, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: the twelve letters used as written

explanation.surface: A tidy-minded host arranges things neatly while the untidiest guests stay in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets order against mess; the messy part is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To systematise is to arrange according to a method or system, putting things in order.
